ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a nitrogen-containing six-membered aromatic ring; the bottom of the ring is positively charged N, and N is connected below to an Ac substituent; on the right side of the figure is a separate carbonyl/enol-like fragment, with O− above and OAc connected on the right, with 1/2 Cu+2 marked next to it and several curved arrows. The curved arrows are ignored according to the problem, and hydrogen-related bonds are not counted. Reasoning count: In the nitrogen-containing six-membered aromatic ring on the left, there are 3 single bonds and 3 double bonds in the ring; counting by bond order gives 3×1 + 3×2 = 9. Add 1 more single bond between N and the Ac substituent, so the left part totals 10. In the right fragment, the C–O− single bond counts as 1, the C=C double bond counts as 2, the C–OAc single bond counts as 1, and the O–Ac connecting single bond counts as 1, so the right part totals 1 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 5. The total is 10 + 5 = 15.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: it contains a left N-containing six-membered ring bearing an Ac substituent and a separate right carbonyl/enolate-like fragment bearing O− and OAc, with curved arrows that must be ignored. Then count bond orders excluding H. For the left component, the aromatic ring has three single C/N–C ring bonds and three double bonds, giving 3 + 6 = 9, and the N–Ac substituent adds 1, so left total is 10. For the right component, count C–O− as 1, C=C as 2, C–OAc as 1, and the O–Ac attachment as 1, giving 5. Sum all components: 10 + 5 = 15.
